title: Hybrid attention profiling diary (Flash + paged + fused ops)
content:
Goal: capture exploratory notes and reproducible commands while we probe a hybrid attention strategy that mixes FlashAttention kernels with paged attention fallbacks and opportunistic fused ops. The aim is to find configurations that reduce p99 tail latency without regressing median throughput for long-tail sequences.

Context / motivation:
- FlashAttention is great for large contiguous sequences but we see variance when request shapes are mixed (short chat turns + occasional 4k+ generations).
- Paged attention (our custom approach: chunk KV into pages, stream from GPU host memory) helps memory-footprint but introduces queuing overhead; fused ops (layer-level kernel fusion) can reduce kernel launch cost but appears brittle when combined with paged I/O.
- Want a reproducible lab notebook with commands, quick numbers, and hypotheses to hand to SRE/infra for follow-up.

Environment:
- HW: p5 instances (A800 equivalent) and c4 (A100-equivalent) in lab cluster. Primary tests on single A800, 80GB.
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (commit: 9a3c7f2), inference-engine v2.1.0-beta, cuquant libs built with nvcc 12.2.
- Models: llama-13b (fp16 orig), quantized 4-bit fallback variant (q4f), sequence lengths tested: 128, 512, 2048, 4096.
- Bench script: tools/bench/bench_attn.py (bench harness that supports --attn-mode {flash,paged,hybrid} and --fused {on,off})

Quick reproducible commands (local lab runner):
- baseline flash: python tools/bench/bench_attn.py --model llama-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --attn-mode flash --fused on --iters 200
- paged only: python tools/bench/bench_attn.py --model llama-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --attn-mode paged --fused off --iters 200
- hybrid: python tools/bench/bench_attn.py --model llama-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --attn-mode hybrid --page-threshold 1024 --fused on --iters 200
- mixed shapes (realistic): python tools/bench/bench_attn.py --model llama-13b --shape-file experiments/mixed_shapes.json --attn-mode hybrid --fused on --iters 1000

Run log highlights (selected):
- 2025-08-12 10:20: baseline flash (seq=2048) median=18.4ms/token, p95=45ms, p99=110ms. Stable across runs.
- 2025-08-12 11:05: paged only (seq=2048) median=20.9ms/token, p95=62ms, p99=190ms. Higher tail due to page faults / host IO.
- 2025-08-13 09:30: hybrid (threshold=1024, fused on) median=18.9ms/token, p95=48ms, p99=120ms. Slight p99 improvement vs pure flash for mixed shapes test.
- 2025-08-14 14:00: hybrid + fused ops aggressive (fuse depth=3) produced rare hard stalls ~1/2000 iterations; host process stacktrace shows nvrtc kernel launch hang. Reproducible with fused depth >=3.

Observed patterns / notes:
1) Memory fragmentation triggers paged fallback more often than expected. After long runs (10k iters) allocator free-list becomes fragmented; paged pages get evicted more frequently -> more host<->device transfers. Suspect our allocator aging heuristics are not coalescing small frees.
2) Fusion helps median by ~5-8% (reduced launches) but amplifies the cost of any single page fault because fused kernel holds more in-flight state and there's less opportunity to interleave IO. When a fused kernel stalls waiting for page load, queue builds and p99 spikes.
3) Hybrid routing threshold matters: threshold too low -> too many flash failures on long sequences; threshold too high -> paged overhead dominates. Empirically threshold ~1k tokens is a reasonable sweet spot for llama-13b on 80GB.
4) KV cache contention: multi-actor workloads (many concurrent small chats) cause KV cache churn. FlashAttention has lower overhead for cache hits; paged model ends up doing more partial reloads. Suggest we add a per-customer LRU hint to bias hot keys to stay resident.
5) NVidia profiling (nvprof/nsight) shows a high number of tiny memcpy ops with paged mode; this dominates wall-clock when IO scheduler is non-optimal. Batching memcpy calls (coalesce adjacent pages) gave ~18% tail reduction in synthetic tests.

Small table (text) of representative numbers (single A800):
- flash seq=512: median=5.2ms, p95=10.1ms, p99=22ms
- flash seq=2048: median=18.4ms, p95=45ms, p99=110ms
- paged seq=2048: median=20.9ms, p95=62ms, p99=190ms
- hybrid (th=1024) mixed shapes: median=12.6ms (weighted), p95=34ms, p99=95ms

Hypotheses / root causes to investigate:
- H1: Allocator fragmentation leads to page eviction frequency growth over long runs. Proof: run long steady-state with allocator metrics exposed; measure eviction rate. Mitigation: run periodic compaction or use a slab allocator for attention pages.
- H2: Fused kernels increase critical section size and thereby increase the cost of any IO stall. Proof: instrument fused vs unfused kernel durations and interleaving gaps. Mitigation: allow partial fusion (fuse only compute-heavy ops, leave IO points unfused) or add cooperative prefetch in fused kernel.
- H3: IO coalescing is suboptimal when multiple small page requests arrive concurrently. Proof: replay workload and measure memcpy counts; try coalescing heuristics. Mitigation: batch page fetches by address range and prefetch heuristic based on seq progression.

Quick experiments to run next (owners noted):
- long-run allocator test (Priya): run 100k iters hybrid with per-alloc hist tracing; dump free-list sizes every 10k iters. Command: python tools/bench/bench_attn.py --model llama-13b --attn-mode hybrid --iters 100000 --trace-allocs
- partial fusion builds (Marcus): compile runtime with FUSE_LEVEL=1 and FUSE_LEVEL=2 kernels; compare stall rates. Link: github PR 492 (work in progress).
- memcpy coalesce patch (Ethan): in pager IO path, implement a 4-page coalesce window; compare p99 on mixed_shapes workload.

Unresolved anomalies / random notes:
- Some hard stalls only appear under cgroups with memory limit set to 60GB (on 80GB card). Suspect kernel-level page reclamation interplay with our device driver mmap. Reproducible on host-OS 6.1 vs 5.15 kernels.
- When fused depth >=3 + quantized int4 model, we saw a subtle numeric regression in sampled outputs (rare token flips). Need to rule out race in accumulation when fusing quant-dequant steps.

Experiment artifacts / where to find full logs:
- bench results: s3://redwood-lab/bench/hybrid-attn/2025-08-12/ (json per-run)
- nsight traces: s3://redwood-lab/trace/hybrid-attn/2025-08-13/
- allocator traces: /var/tmp/alloc-trace-ava/ (local lab node)

Decisions / interim config recommendation for service branch (if we need to stabilise quickly):
- Default to hybrid mode with page-threshold=1024, fused:on but FUSE_LEVEL=1 (less aggressive).
- Enable memcpy coalescing in pager IO (Ethan patch staged) so that small seq bursts benefit immediately.
- Add an experiment flag --alloc-compact to bench harness to trigger compaction after warmup; evaluate effect.

Action items (short):
- [Priya] run allocator long-run and upload traces by 2025-08-18.
- [Marcus] land partial-fusion builder and push perf matrix by 2025-08-22.
- [Ethan] finish memcpy coalesce and test on mixed_shapes by 2025-08-20.
- [Ava] reproduce hard stalls on cgroup-limited VMs and capture kernel logs by 2025-08-19.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Consider exposing a runtime knob for "fusion optimism" that gates fusion on observed page-residency ratio. Could dynamically disable fusion when eviction rate spikes.
- Write a small microbench that synthesizes many small interleaved requests to stress the pager; use it as unit test in CI.

References / prior docs:
- attention-kernel-exploration-notes.json (related but different scope)
- paging design doc (confluence) - see linked_artifacts URL above

End diary entry. Keep incremental notes here; this doc will hold raw logs and evolving hypotheses until we have a consolidated playbook.

(roughly a mix of quick findings + TODOs — expect this to be noisy; will formalize into a playbook once MEM fragmentation and fused-stall causes are pinned.)
